issues.legal_issue: A prior statement may not be used against a witness as an admission when it concerns an unrelated issue, is not a clear admission, or is not put to the witness for an opportunity to explain it before it is proved.
material_facts: The earlier deposition concerned a dispute over different survey numbers from those at issue in the later proceeding.
Read as a whole, the deposition did not clearly admit a landlord-tenant relationship; it stated that no rent was received and that the land was fallow.
The witness was not shown the deposition during cross-examination, and a certified copy was placed on record after his evidence had concluded.
issues.conclusion: The earlier deposition was not a usable admission against the witness, and the argument that he was bound by it was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 17 of the Indian Evidence Act, an admission must concern a fact in issue or relevant fact. Admissions must be clear to be used against their maker; under section 145, a witness must be given an opportunity to address a writing intended to contradict him. The Court applied Bharat Singh v. Bhagirathi and Bal Gangadhar Tilak v. Shrinivas Pandit, including the principle that a witness should see and be able to answer a statement before it is used against him.

rule.if: prior_statement_offered_as_admission and (statement_concerned_unrelated_issue or statement_was_ambiguous or witness_not_confronted_before_proof)

predicates.prior_statement_offered_as_admission: A party offered an earlier statement made by a witness as an admission against that witness.
predicates.statement_concerned_unrelated_issue: The earlier statement concerned a matter that was neither in issue nor relevant in the proceeding where it was offered.
predicates.statement_was_ambiguous: The earlier statement, read in context, did not clearly and unequivocally admit the fact for which it was offered.
predicates.witness_not_confronted_before_proof: The witness was not shown the statement and given an opportunity to explain it before it was proved and relied on against the witness.
predicates.prior_statement_not_used_against_witness: The earlier statement is not used against its maker as an admission.

issues.definition: When an earlier statement offered as an admission is unrelated, ambiguous, or not put to its maker for an opportunity to respond before proof, it is not used against that maker.

issues.legal_issue: Entries in a record of rights are not presumed correct when the evidence establishes that they are inaccurate, and the presumption may also be unavailable where the affected person received no notice of the mutation proceedings.
material_facts: The record of rights listed the claimant as a tenant, but the fact-finding authorities concluded from the evidence that he had not cultivated the land as a tenant.
The entries contained indications inconsistent with the actual state of affairs, and the oral evidence contradicted them.
The entries related to mutation proceedings of which the respondent had received no notice.
issues.conclusion: The record-of-rights entries did not establish tenancy and could not validly carry a presumption of correctness in the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Section 135-J of the Bombay Land Revenue Code gives a record of rights presumptive value, but there is no abstract rule that every entry must be treated as correct; evidence showing that an entry is inaccurate can displace the presumption. The Court also relied on the conflicting evidence and the absence of notice of the mutation proceedings.

rule.if: tenancy_status_proceeding and record_entries_relied_on and (evidence_contradicted_entries or mutation_proceeding_without_notice)

predicates.tenancy_status_proceeding: The proceeding required a determination of whether a person held land as a tenant.
predicates.record_entries_relied_on: A party relied on official record entries as evidence of the claimed status.
predicates.evidence_contradicted_entries: Evidence before the decision-maker showed that the record entries did not reflect the actual state of affairs.
predicates.mutation_proceeding_without_notice: The person affected by the entries received no notice of the mutation proceeding that produced them.
predicates.record_entries_not_presumed_correct: The entries are not treated as presumptively correct to establish the claimed status.

issues.definition: In a proceeding about tenancy status, relied-on record entries are not presumed correct when the evidence contradicts them or the affected person received no notice of the mutation proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A revisional tribunal cannot set aside concurrent factual findings merely because it would assess the evidence differently when the lower authorities considered the evidence and no error of law appears on the face of the record.
material_facts: The Mamlatdar and Deputy Collector both considered the evidence and found that the claimant had not cultivated the land as a tenant.
The Revenue Tribunal revisited the evidentiary assessment and treated the lower authorities as having wrongly placed the burden of proof on the claimant.
The Tribunal identified no error of law on the face of the record; the High Court set aside its decision.
issues.conclusion: The Revenue Tribunal had no jurisdiction to interfere with the concurrent factual findings, and the challenge to the High Court's decision was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Section 76 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act limits the grounds for revision, including error of law. Where the authority entrusted with fact-finding has assessed the evidence, its decision being right or wrong does not itself establish an error of law on the face of the record. When the entire evidence is before the court, the burden of proof becomes immaterial.

rule.if: statutory_revision_proceeding and lower_authorities_assessed_evidence and revisional_body_reweighed_facts and no_error_of_law_on_record

predicates.statutory_revision_proceeding: A party invoked a statutory revisional proceeding to challenge findings made by lower fact-finding authorities.
predicates.lower_authorities_assessed_evidence: The lower authorities considered the evidence and made factual findings.
predicates.revisional_body_reweighed_facts: The revisional body reconsidered the evidence or its weight to reach a different factual conclusion.
predicates.no_error_of_law_on_record: The record disclosed no error of law apparent on its face in the lower authorities' decision.
predicates.revisional_body_cannot_set_aside_concurr: The revisional body cannot overturn the concurrent factual findings on that basis.

issues.definition: When lower authorities have assessed the evidence and a revisional body merely reweighs it without an error of law apparent on the record, the revisional body cannot set aside their concurrent factual findings.
